rules_evaluated.evidence: DEFINITIONAL CONTRACT — holds. The sibling's five facets (what-is-an-agent.md lines 11-17: multi-step work, context, tools, goal, bounded autonomy) map onto this file's four parts (context, tools, goal, autonomy) exactly as before: the 'Four parts:' enumeration sentence is byte-identical pre- and post-edit (git show 91afed4 touches only the head clause 'An agent is an LLM [in a loop -> calling tools in a loop]', never the four-parts list). The maintainer's three standing rules all still hold: (a) list not re-cut — 'context, tools, goal, autonomy' unchanged; (b) context and goal both still present; (c) autonomy still narrower-than-sibling by design, untouched. The phrase carrying multi-step work, 'in a loop', is still present verbatim post-edit — the contract's literal anchor survives. One real, non-blocking wrinkle the new grammar introduces: 'in a loop' now scopes over 'calling tools' (an LLM [calling tools] [in a loop]) rather than over 'an LLM' broadly (an LLM [in a loop]), narrowing the phrase from 'the LLM's whole operation iterates' to 'the LLM's tool-calling iterates'. Bullet 1's own third sentence ('each iteration... either responds to you or uses tools') concedes not every iteration calls a tool, which sits in mild tension with a headline that now foregrounds tool-calling as the defining activity — a seam that didn't exist under the plainer 'an LLM in a loop' headline. It resolves within the same slide (bullet 3: the loop runs 'until the agent decides to stop', which covers the no-tool-call/respond-only branch) and doesn't threaten the sibling contract, the four-parts list, or the mood floor — recorded as a TODO, not a REVISE. FRONT-RUN CHECK: body carries only vocabulary + tool-list mechanism; maintainer block explicitly guards against M3/M5 vocabulary leaking in ('no packaging laws... stay out until M5', 'no "one loop, three sizes" naming (M3's beat)') — unaffected by today's edit. MODULE-TO-MODULE ARC: verified via git show 91afed4 -- run-the-first-experiment.md — the module's 'Start here' lead-in line was synced in the SAME commit ('Next, the thing you are sending: an LLM calling tools in a loop.'), so the module body and this lecture's headline now echo each other exactly rather than drifting; the hand-off is tighter after the edit, not looser. BIG IDEA FIDELITY: M4's Big Idea (walk what you've built, send un-packaged, learn from what the agent does) is honoured — bullet 4 and the tool-list prompt still ground the exact mechanism and surface the exact tool set the send-off will carry; today's edit touches none of that. MOOD-DOESN'T-RESOLVE-EARLY: no touch on M5's 'learning through contrast' vocabulary, no over-resolution of M4's own curious-readiness ahead of the exercise.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Narrow-lens suggestion only, not a recipe: if the same-bullet grammar seam is worth closing, the fix is local to bullet 1's own third sentence, not the headline — e.g. naming that a tool-call is what USUALLY closes an iteration, with a plain reply as the loop's exit condition, so 'calling tools in a loop' and 'either responds to you or uses tools' read as the rule and its one named exception rather than two competing claims about what the loop is for.
